The issue is that the `Panel` title is not being styled with the panel's background style when rendered. The `__rich_console__` method calculates the overall `style` and `border_style` but does not apply the `style` to the title or subtitle when they are rendered within the panel structure.

I will modify `rich/panel.py` to ensure that the title and subtitle are styled with the panel's main style.

I need to check how the title and subtitle are used in the rendering process. Since `__rich_console__` is the entry point for rendering, I suspect the styling needs to be applied there or in a helper method that uses the calculated styles.

Looking at the structure, the `Panel` object itself doesn't seem to handle the final rendering of the title text, but rather provides the data (`self.title`, `self.subtitle`) and configuration (`self.style`, `self.border_style`).

If the title is missing the background style, it means the `Text` object returned by `_title` is not being passed the correct style when it is eventually rendered by the console.

I will modify `__rich_console__` to pass the calculated `style` to the title and subtitle if they exist, assuming the rendering logic downstream uses the `style` attribute of the `Panel` object or the `Text` object itself.

However, since `_title` returns a `Text` object, I should probably ensure that the `Text` object is styled correctly before it is used.

Let's look at `_title` again. It returns a `Text` object. If I modify `_title` to apply the style, it would be cleaner. But `_title` doesn't have access to `self.style` directly in a way that allows applying it to the returned `Text` object unless I pass it in or access it.

The `Panel` object has `self.style`.

If I modify `_title` to apply the style:

```python
    @property
    def _title(self) -> Optional[Text]:
        if self.title:
            title_text = (
                Text.from_markup(self.title)
                if isinstance(self.title, str)
                else self.title.copy()
            )
            title_text.end = ""
            title_text.plain = title_text.plain.replace("\\n", " ")
            title_text.no_wrap = True
            title_text.expand_tabs()
            title_text.pad(1)
            title_text.style = self.style # <-- Add this line
            return title_text
        return None
```
This seems like the most direct fix for the title missing the style. I will apply this change to `rich/panel.py`.
